objective: Match a subsequence using the same Unicode code-point unit in both strings.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Text traversal remains routine JavaScript work.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Consistent character units prevent contradictory implementations.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Surrogate pairs, lone surrogates and explicit normalization policy transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The third stage combines earlier functions with bounded string iteration.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: The original boards disagreed on valid emoji input.

defects: Reference/senior iterated big by code point but indexed small by UTF-16 code unit.
Junior indexed both strings by code unit, so boards disagreed on emoji/half-surrogate inputs.
The original hint repeated the mixed-unit defect and input-size meaning was unstated.
rationale: Choose code points as yielded by for...of for both inputs, including lone surrogates, with separate combining marks and no normalization. Strings are primitive and at most20000 UTF-16 units each; n is their total unit length, m is small code-point count. State O(n) time/O(m) extra space and allow constant-space streaming. Reference/senior materialize wanted code points; junior advances big by codePointAt width. Correct the hint/approach. Add one visible emoji and three hidden assertions:1600 generated-string pairs checked by an independent two-dimensional subsequence DP, explicit paired/lone-surrogate/no-normalization cases, and20000-unit boundaries. The streaming-wanted iterator alternative passes; the old mixed-unit strategy passed all ASCII checks and now fails. The original actual worker probe records reference/senior false,false versus junior true,true for full-emoji and half-surrogate queries.
